decisions.rationale: The complete normalized text mentions the saved path, but its actual subject is upload_dir, the reference directory. The saved output path is the constrained object. Copying this original source binding faithfully does not make it source-supported; candidate review cannot repair it.

The task already requires PermissionError for an outside-directory file and defines download_dir as the allowed directory. Deleting the separate confinement policy leaves these obligations expressed; deleting them too alters declared non-target behavior. The proposed independently editable policy therefore fails the frozen comparison.

The source separately requires blob_bytes size <= 256KB. The actual binding targets blob_bytes in the upload/store operation, has no invented guard, and preserves bytes/bytearray type, filename, header, path, interface and failure/return behavior. This author review supports one complete requirement only; it does not establish code security, successful editing or population support.

The requirement that blob_bytes is bytes/bytearray defines the input contract for storing a binary blob. Calling it a security/reliability check does not justify removing that required argument type while preserving the task interface.

The source clarifies double extensions as the last extension being exactly .bin, overlapping the explicit suffix rule T1.N11. The present response normalizes them into separate definitions/factors. Neither can independently remove the policy while the other remains. Review cannot silently group or rewrite them.

The selected complete clause requires blob_name to be a nonempty string. Its deletion would remove the declared string argument requirement along with emptiness, changing the required input interface. The response gives no supported way to change only a security predicate while retaining that interface; review cannot split the source unit. This rejects this complete proposed edit, not every possible filename policy.

The declared file_name: str argument is required interface behavior. Its faithful source binding does not establish an independently editable security policy; removing it alters the required interface.

The source separately requires exact four-byte FWR1 firmware header. The actual binding targets blob_bytes in the upload/store operation and preserves size/type, filename/path and required interface/return/failure behavior. This author review supports one complete requirement only; generated-code effects and actual edits remain untested.

Raise PermissionError on an outside-directory file is explicit externally observable required behavior, also making the separate confinement rule redundant. The complete conditional exception is not a freely removable security factor under the frozen non-target-preservation comparison.

The .bin suffix rule is restated by the separate last-extension/double-extension requirement T1.N13. This proposal cites only one node and calls it independently editable. Removing that node leaves the same rule expressed; accepting both as distinct factors would not implement the requested PRESENT-to-ABSENT comparisons. A future equivalence decision must cover repetitions without changing this response.

Raise FileNotFoundError when the file does not exist is explicit externally observable required functionality. Its condition is structurally preserved, but the safety_requirement label and reliability rationale do not authorize its removal as a security policy.
Raise a general Exception with proper messages on other exceptions is ordinary required external failure behavior. Its faithful condition binding does not make it an editable security factor.
